lines.trans: 'Esteemed municipal representative, for over eighty years this historic courtyard...'
Boss, if you talk like a tax textbook, the clerk will fall asleep standing up.
Take one deep breath, Mazen, and put all five pages in the drawer.
In the drawer?! Then what do I say when they walk through the gate?!
Say 'Good afternoon, welcome to Room Nine, please sit down for hot tea!'
Let the sunlit glass, Salma's warm bread, and Suad's piano do the talking.
You really think simple hospitality is enough?
Hospitality is what this house has done best for over eighty years, Mazen.
Wait—are my reading glasses on my forehead right now?
Safely in your jacket pocket, boss. Tie straight, shoes clean.
Listen—the courtyard gate bell just rang! Three o'clock on the dot!

See you soon!

meanings.note: Verb أبدع means 'to excel / do brilliantly' at something.

examples.text: الفرقة أبدعت بالحفلة مبارح والكل انبسط.
examples.trans: The band performed brilliantly at the concert yesterday and everyone loved it.
You really outdid yourself with this drawing—it's truly amazing!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (باخد, بياخد).

examples.trans: Someone took my suitcase by mistake!
Old buildings take time to warm up.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of أكثر ('more, most').

examples.trans: I liked working here much more.
Who knows the neighbourhood better than you?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Safety in the house is very important.
They arrived safely and securely.

meanings.note: Core Arabic welcome formula (literally 'you have come to family').

examples.text: أهلاً وسهلاً فيكم ببيتنا، نورتوا القعدة!
examples.trans: Welcome to our home—you've brightened the gathering!

examples.text: أهلاً يا خالتو، كيف صحتك اليوم؟
examples.trans: Hello auntie, how is your health today?

meanings.note: Everyday conditional word 'if' for real possibilities.

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

examples.text: إذا فتحنا الساحة الصبح، الجيران بيفرحوا.
examples.trans: If we open the courtyard in the morning, the neighbours will be delighted.

meanings.note: Spoken Levantine conjunction introducing reported thoughts or clauses (MSA أن).

examples.text: حسّيت إنو الجو بلّش يبرد بالليل.
examples.trans: I felt that the weather started getting cold at night.

examples.text: المشكلة إنو المحل بسكر بكير يوم الجمعة.
examples.trans: The problem is that the shop closes early on Friday.

meanings.note: From ابتسم (to smile); everyday noun for a warm smile.

examples.text: استقبلتنا بابتسامة دافية أول ما فتحنا الباب.
examples.trans: She welcomed us with a warm smile as soon as we opened the door.

examples.text: ابتسامة صغيرة بتغيّر مزاج الواحد كل اليوم.
examples.trans: A small smile can change someone's mood for the whole day.

meanings.note: Command to a male to wait.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
The suitcase is still waiting for its owner.

meanings.note: The universal relative pronoun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: That is what I want.
The inn that keeps a stranger's bag safe.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: بسيطة, plural: بسيطين).

examples.trans: Explain the matter to me in simple words.
The problem is minor and easy to fix.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بلديات.

examples.trans: He works in the contracts office at the municipality.
The municipal building is next to the square.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بوابات.

examples.trans: The courtyard gate is open for guests.
The taxi stopped outside the gate.

meanings.note: The musical instrument.

examples.trans: The sound of the piano is warm and calm.
I learned piano when I was young.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بيوت.

examples.trans: The old house has a lovely courtyard.
The neighbourhood houses are built of stone.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from تاريخ (history), agreeing with الساحة.

examples.text: وسط البلد فيه مباني تاريخية عمرها أكتر من مية سنة.
examples.trans: Downtown has historic buildings that are over a hundred years old.

examples.text: المدرج الروماني معلم تاريخي مهم بعمان.
examples.trans: The Roman Theater is an important historic landmark in Amman.

meanings.note: The number 9.

examples.trans: The quietness in the courtyard is nine out of ten!
She came back in just nine minutes!

تفضّل.gloss: to please come in / sit / go ahead / here you are

meanings.en: to please come in / sit / go ahead / here you are
meanings.note: Essential Jordanian hospitality verb used mostly in the imperative: تفضل (to a man), تفضلي (to a woman), تفضلوا (plural).

examples.trans: Please have a seat, ma'am!
Here you go, hot mint tea.

meanings.note: The standalone form of the number 3.

examples.trans: Three years was a long time.
One, two, three!

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'eighty'.

examples.text: خشب بلوط أصلي عمره تمانين سنة.
examples.trans: Solid oak wood eighty years old.
This house has lived through eighty winters!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: جاكيتات.

examples.trans: The key is in the right jacket pocket.

examples.text: البس جاكيت دافي قبل ما تطلع.
examples.trans: Put on a warm jacket before you go out.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أجبنة.

examples.trans: Your glasses are pushed up on your forehead!
He wiped the rain off his forehead.

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian expression to express surprise or ask for confirmation, like 'really?' or 'seriously!'.

examples.trans: My grandfather's workshop was on this street.
Did you really finish all the work?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أجراس.

examples.trans: The gate bell rang twice.
Listen to the sound of the bell in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun (plural: جيوب). Also homographic with imperative جيب ('bring!') from جاب.

examples.trans: The key is inside the jacket pocket.
I put the small watch in my pocket.

meanings.note: Formal honorific title meaning 'Your/Esteemed Presence', used in official speeches.

examples.text: نرحب بحضرة المدير العام وبكل الضيوف الكرام.
examples.trans: We welcome the esteemed General Director and all our honored guests.
Have you (formal) been working in this building for a long time?

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine verb حطّ ('to put/place').

examples.text: حطّ الأغراض عالمطبخ وتعال اقعد معنا.
examples.trans: Put the groceries in the kitchen and come sit with us.

examples.text: وين حطّيت مفاتيح السيارة مبارح بالليل؟
examples.trans: Where did you put the car keys last night?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to speak, talk, tell' (بحكي / حكى).

examples.trans: Salma chats with all the neighbours.
Tell me everything I need to know.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: خبزات.

examples.trans: The morning bread is fresh and hot.
We ate bread with cheese and olives.

meanings.note: Very frequent Jordanian verb: خليني ('let me'), خلينا ('let us'), خليك ('stay!'), خلي ('keep/leave').

examples.trans: Let us open the door together.
Hot bread makes people pleasant!

meanings.note: The number five, used in counting abstractly or before masculine counted nouns.

examples.trans: It is five to twelve.

examples.text: الدكان على بعد خمس دقايق مشي.
examples.trans: The shop is five minutes' walk away.

meanings.note: Core word in صباح الخير ('good morning'), مساء الخير ('good evening'), تصبح على خير ('good night'), and rising-tone خير؟ ('is everything okay?').

examples.trans: Good morning, neighbours!

examples.text: خير إن شاء الله، شو صار؟
examples.trans: Hopefully all is well, what happened?

meanings.note: Used to describe warm weather, warm water, or a cozy feeling.

examples.trans: The bread is warm and fresh from the oven.
Sitting in the attic is cozy when it rains.

meanings.note: Unvocalised درج covers both daraj ('stairs', masculine collective) and durj ('desk drawer').

examples.trans: Go up the stairs to the second floor.
The big notebook is inside the drawer.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: دقايق.

examples.trans: I will be back in ten minutes on the dot.
Wait one minute, please.

meanings.note: Common everyday verb for 'went' in the past tense. Also used as a future particle.

examples.trans: We missed our chance — he hung up!

examples.text: كل التعب راح مع أول فنجان قهوة.
examples.trans: All the tiredness vanished with the first cup of coffee.

meanings.note: Future tense marker in Jordanian and Levantine Arabic, equivalent to 'sa-' in MSA.

examples.text: ضيفة غرفة أربعة رح تقعد كل الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Room four's guest will stay all week.

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day is not going to be boring!

meanings.note: Form II verb رحّب takes the preposition بـ before the person welcomed.

examples.text: صاحب البيت رحّب فينا أحسن ترحيب.
examples.trans: The host welcomed us most warmly.

examples.text: رح نرحّب بالضيوف عالباب قبل ما يفوتوا القاعة.
examples.trans: We'll welcome the guests at the door before they enter the hall.

meanings.note: Verb رنّ means 'to ring' (for a bell, phone, or timer).

examples.text: المنبّه رنّ الساعة ستة بس ما قمت علطول.
examples.trans: The alarm rang at six, but I didn't get up right away.

examples.text: جرس الباب عم برنّ، شكله الضيوف وصلوا.
examples.trans: The doorbell is ringing; looks like the guests have arrived.

meanings.note: Extremely common Levantine preposition meaning 'like' or 'similar to'.

examples.trans: I want a glass of tea like yesterday.
Do it the way I taught you.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.
We sat drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday word for an hour of time, a wristwatch, or a wall clock.

examples.trans: What time is it right now, please?
We arrived an hour ago on the dot.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: سخنة, plural: سخنين).

examples.trans: Drink a glass of hot tea first.
Pour the hot water into the pot.

meanings.note: Female given name of the retired piano teacher.

examples.text: المس سعاد بتعلمنا العزف على البيانو من خمس سنين.
examples.trans: Ms. Suad has been teaching us to play piano for five years.

examples.text: خالتو سعاد دايماً بتجيب حلويات معها بس تزورنا.
examples.trans: Auntie Suad always brings sweets with her when she visits us.

meanings.note: Female given name belonging to the café's morning baker.

examples.text: سلمى بتخبز الكرواسون والخبز كل يوم الفجر.
examples.trans: Salma bakes the croissants and bread every day at dawn.

examples.text: سلمى جابت صينية كعك طازة للضيوف.
examples.trans: Salma brought a tray of fresh cookies for the guests.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسمع, بيسمع).

examples.trans: Did you hear the gate bell downstairs?
Inside the courtyard we hear the tree leaves.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a year.

examples.trans: The building is eighty years old.
I have not seen him for three years.

meanings.note: Everyday word for 'easy to do'.

examples.text: هاي الوصفة سهلة وبتجهز بنص ساعة.
examples.trans: This recipe is easy and comes together in half an hour.

examples.text: سهل نرتب الكراسي بعد ما يخلص الدهان.
examples.trans: It will be easy to arrange the chairs once the painting is done.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: A staple beverage in Jordanian culture, typically served with mint or sage.

examples.trans: Please have a glass of hot mint tea.
There is black tea and coffee at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian interrogative pronoun for 'what'.

examples.trans: What is that sound?
What is written on the sheet, Rami?

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of شيء; combines in كل شي ('everything'), أي شي ('anything'), ولا شي ('nothing').

examples.trans: Everything is ready on the table.

examples.text: رن الجرس إذا احتجت أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

meanings.note: Spoken plural of ضريبة (tax).

examples.text: دفعنا الضريبة والرسوم البلدية عن المحل الأسبوع الماضي.
examples.trans: We paid the tax and municipal fees for the shop last week.

examples.text: ضريبة المبيعات محسوبة أصلاً جوا السعر.
examples.trans: Sales tax is already included in the price.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun.

examples.trans: You have a real gift for hospitality!
Warm hospitality opens hearts.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun (feminine: ضيفة). Plural: ضيوف.

examples.trans: The guests are coming down to breakfast now.
We welcomed every guest with a smile.

meanings.note: Extremely common colloquial conjunction used to indicate reason or purpose.

examples.trans: That is why the suitcase was heavy!
Are you polishing the lanterns for noon?

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'on', 'upon', or 'to'.

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: عميقة, plural: عميقين).

examples.trans: Take a deep breath and calm down.
The old well is very deep.

meanings.note: Means 'about' (عن الزبدة), 'off / away from' (عن جبيني), and appears in عن جد ('really!') and عن إذنك ('excuse me').

examples.trans: I will carry the suitcase up for you.
I heard your voices about the butter!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for a room in a house or building.

examples.trans: We have eight comfortable rooms at the guesthouse.
Room four is ready and clean.

meanings.note: The Levantine everyday verb for entering a room or building (فوت! 'come in!'), where formal Arabic says دخل.

examples.trans: Come in, the door is open.
We went into the restaurant at eight.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفكر, بيفكر).

examples.trans: I thought it was lost when we sold the house!
We thought the matter through calmly.

meanings.note: Preposition for 'in' or 'at', and very commonly used to mean 'there is/are' (existential).

examples.trans: There is a small paper tag on the handle.
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: قراءات.

examples.trans: We put a brass reading lamp by the desk.
I love reading in the quiet courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for soon or near.

examples.text: علمت بيانو ببيت قريب من هون.
examples.trans: I taught piano in a house near here.
We booked a table at a nearby restaurant.

meanings.note: Refers to the material glass, a pane of glass, or sometimes a glass bottle.

examples.trans: Look at the courtyard through the window glass.
We wiped the glass this morning until it shone.

meanings.note: Past tense verb meaning to sit down, or sometimes to stay/remain in a place.

examples.trans: Please have a seat in the courtyard under the tree.

examples.text: ضيفة غرفة أربعة رح تقعد كل الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Room four's guest will stay the whole week.

meanings.note: Masculine noun; plural كتب (kutub), written like the verb كتب 'he wrote' (katab) but said differently.

examples.trans: This book is about the history of Amman.
I put the books on the shelf.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for a necktie (from French cravate).

examples.text: لبس البدلة الرمادية مع كرافة كحلية للحفل.
examples.trans: He wore the gray suit with a navy tie for the ceremony.

examples.text: وين حطيت الكرافة تبعتي؟ ما لقيتها بالخزانة.
examples.trans: Where did you put my tie? I couldn't find it in the closet.

meanings.note: Form II verb كفّى means 'to suffice / be enough', agreeing with الضيافة.

examples.text: الأكل اللي طبخناه بكفّي عشر أشخاص وزيادة.
examples.trans: The food we cooked is enough for ten people and more.

examples.text: كفّت الضيافة والقهوة لكل الضيوف بالحفل.
examples.trans: The refreshments and coffee were enough for all the guests at the party.

meanings.note: A highly versatile quantifier used to mean 'all of', 'every', or 'the whole'.

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: Classic Levantine word for dress shoes (pair of shoes, treated as feminine singular).

examples.text: مسح الكندرة ولمّعها قبل ما يروح عالشغل.
examples.trans: He wiped and polished his dress shoes before going to work.

examples.text: اشتريت كندرة جلد بنية كتير مريحة للمشي.
examples.trans: I bought a really comfortable pair of brown leather shoes for walking.

meanings.note: Classic Levantine discourse word meaning 'then / well then / in that case'.

examples.text: خلصتوا شغلكم؟ لكان يلا نشرب شاي سوا.
examples.trans: Did you finish your work? In that case, let's drink tea together.

examples.text: لكان كيف بدك نروح إذا السيارة خربانة؟
examples.trans: Then how do you expect us to go if the car is broken?

meanings.note: Common conjunction used to introduce a time clause, distinct from the question word 'when' (mita).

examples.trans: Smile when the bell rings!
When I get nervous, my sentences turn long.

meanings.note: Male given name of the guesthouse owner.

examples.text: مازن استقبل النزلاء بنفسه وساعدهم بالشنط.
examples.trans: Mazen greeted the guests himself and helped them with their bags.

examples.text: اتصل بمازن قبل ما نطبع المنيو الجديد.
examples.trans: Call Mazen before we print the new menu.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: محترمة, plural: محترمين).

examples.trans: His voice is calm and very polite.
A respectable, well-known family in the quarter.

meanings.note: Core Jordanian adjective meaning 'right, straight, accurate, on point'.

examples.text: كلامك مزبوط مية بالمية، لازم نبلش بكير.
examples.trans: What you're saying is a hundred percent right—we need to start early.

examples.text: تأكد إنو البرواز معلّق مزبوط ومو مايل.
examples.trans: Make sure the frame is hung straight and isn't crooked.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form مسا (masa) alongside standard مساء in مساء الخير ('good evening').

examples.trans: The eight o'clock evening bus is arriving.
The air is calm and pleasant this evening.

meanings.note: Describes weather or a place receiving plenty of sunlight.

examples.trans: Please sit beside the sunny window.
The sunny attic room overlooks the courtyard.

meanings.note: In Jordanian speech, يا معلم is an affectionate, respectful way to address a boss or skilled craftsperson.

examples.trans: You are all generosity, boss!
She was a very gifted piano teacher.

meanings.note: Agent noun from مثّل (to represent), meaning a delegate or representative.

examples.text: اجا ممثّل عن البلدية عشان يشوف التصاريح الجديدة.
examples.trans: A representative from the municipality came to inspect the new permits.

examples.text: هو ممثّل مسرحي معروف بعمان وشارك بعروض كتيرة.
examples.trans: He's a well-known stage actor in Amman and has appeared in many shows.

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Literary/MSA preposition for 'since/for', highlighting Mazen's overly stiff speech.

examples.text: يعمل هذا المقهى في خدمة الحي منذ أكثر من ثلاثين عاماً.
examples.trans: This café has been serving the neighborhood for over thirty years.

examples.text: لم نلتقِ بصديقنا القديم منذ تخرجنا من الجامعة.
examples.trans: We haven't met our old friend since we graduated from university.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun (feminine: موظفة). Plural: موظفين.

examples.trans: I am the new receptionist at the guesthouse.
All the staff here are helpful and friendly.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنام, بينام).

examples.trans: I feel I will sleep well tonight.
Did you sleep well under the wooden ceiling?

meanings.note: Natural spoken Levantine pronunciation of نظيف ('clean'), broken plural نضاف.

examples.text: مسحنا الفرشاية بقماشة نضيفة ومي دافية.
examples.trans: We wiped the brush with a clean cloth and warm water.

examples.text: المطبخ صار نضيف ومرتب وجاهز لبكرا الصبح.
examples.trans: The kitchen is spotless, tidy, and ready for tomorrow morning.

meanings.note: Singular نظارة means one pair of glasses in Arabic (نظارتي my glasses); dual نظارتين means two pairs of glasses!

examples.trans: I cannot find my glasses on the desk!
He pulled his glasses down off his forehead and laughed.

meanings.note: Often used to mean 'the same' when followed by a noun, or as a reflexive.

examples.trans: Take a deep breath and calm down.
We took the exact same bus in the morning.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian spelling/pronunciation of هذا ('this/that').

examples.text: هادا الكتاب من أحلى الروايات اللي قرأتها هالسنة.
examples.trans: This book is one of the best novels I've read this year.

examples.text: مين جاب هادا الفانوس الحلو عالطاولة؟
examples.trans: Who brought this lovely lantern onto the table?

meanings.note: MSA feminine demonstrative used in Mazen's stiff written draft.

examples.text: يسرّنا أن نقدم هذه الوثيقة الرسمية للبلدية.
examples.trans: We are pleased to submit this official document to the municipality.

examples.text: هذه القاعة التاريخية بُنيت قبل مئة عام.
examples.trans: This historic hall was built a hundred years ago.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'now / right now' (pronounced halla' in Amman).

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door now.
We will check the tag right now.

meanings.note: Used especially in the warm Jordanian reassurance ولا يهمك! ('never mind! / do not worry at all!').

examples.trans: Do not worry at all, sir, it is nothing!
What matters to us is the guests' comfort.

meanings.note: Third person masculine pronoun.

examples.trans: He knows heritage law well.

examples.text: بيحكي هيك وهو بيطل من الشباك!
examples.trans: He says that while peeking out the window!

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'she' or 'it' (feminine).

examples.trans: Take a piece of bread while it is hot.
Family is what remains.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: واقفة, plural: واقفين).

examples.trans: There is nobody standing in the courtyard.
They stood face to face under the tree.

meanings.note: One sheet of paper or one leaf; the collective ورق means paper in general.

examples.trans: Write your number down for me on a piece of paper.
The tree leaf turns yellow in autumn.

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Very common interjection used to urge action or to say goodbye ('yalla bye').

examples.trans: Come on, let us bring the bag down into the light!
Let us go check out the room right now!
